reason: My sister-in-law in Karachi and my cousin in Dubai send me thobes and abayas every season, and when I go to Istanbul I fill a suitcase for less than what one of these jalabiya sets costs here. I don't need another store, and $75 to $80 for a crepe thobe is what I'd pay for two or three back home.
objection: Crepe at this price is often thin and clingy, and I can't tell from an ad whether it's see-through in daylight or scratchy at the embroidery. I'm not driving up to Westheimer on a weekday just to feel fabric I can get cheaper through family.
would_change_my_mind: A last-minute need, like a wedding or henna night coming up before my relatives' parcel arrives, and a friend telling me the crepe is thick and lined. Then I'd go for the thobe plus Layla Bisht deal.
